text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed lower on origin selling and profit taking in response to New York's setback on Friday. March lost $52 to close at $1,600 per tonne, while May gave up $62 to close at $1,615 per tonne. Further losses are not excluded but that will also depend on performance in New York, which was closed on Monday.

All eyes are now fixed on the US Green Coffee Association stock report due on Tuesday. The meeting of Central American members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to discuss export quota allocation is expected to be routine and is not likely to have any market impact.
News LIFFE's certified stock data showed a jump to 2,831 5-tonne lots in January from 1,875 lots in December was largely ignored by the market.

ACPC - Central American members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) held a meeting in Honduras on Monday, to analyze why world prices have spiked so sharply. There was talk that Central American nations are seeking to loosen the ACPC's grip on exports because of the recent steep rise of world market prices and that this meeting would thrash out a less rigid proposal for the full ACPC council to consider. The regional meeting has no definite decision making capacity within the ACPC.

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings for the week ended February 8 totalled approximately 425,000 60-kg bags, up from 400,000 bags the previous week and compared to 410,000 bags in the corresponding week a year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 2.290 million 60-kg bags, versus 2.220 million bags in the same year-ago period.

UNITED KINGDOM - The UK imported 202,673 bags of coffee in November 1996, 11 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 2.708 million bags, 4.9 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 18 per cent to 2.783 million bags.

Main suppliers of green coffee in January/November 1996 were Costa Rica (228,800 vs 317,700 bags), Colombia (243,300 vs 183,200 bags) and Indonesia (344,100 vs 254,500 bags). The country exported 496,200 bags of coffee in January/November 1996, 1.5 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 20 per cent to 538,400 bags.
